contributions.headingText: Pulmonary artery intimal sarcoma is a malignant mesenchymal tumour arising in the large vessels of the pulmonary circulation with predominantly intraluminal growth, obstruction of the lumen of the vessel of origin, and seeding of emboli to peripheral organs.
2C25.Y & XH36H7 Other specified malignant neoplasms of bronchus or lung & Intimal sarcoma

Pulmonary artery intimal sarcomas occur in the proximal elastic arteries, from the level of the pulmonary valve to the lobar branches. Most cases have bilateral involvement, although one side is usually dominant {3055809; 8448740}. Cardiac involvement occurs in some cases {24625414; 26725181}.

The most common presenting symptom is dyspnoea, followed by chest or back pain, cough, haemoptysis, weight loss, malaise, syncope, and fever. The clinical manifestations mimic those of acute or chronic thromboembolism and pulmonary hypertension, because of obstruction of the pulmonary circulation {8989065}. Recurrent pulmonary embolic disease is the most common primary diagnosis, with diagnosis of malignancy often delayed or made after death.

Imaging

Imaging is largely nonspecific; however, the neoplastic nature of the tissue occluding the lumen can be suspected on CT, MRI, or PET {29962886; 28912665; 21607843; 19462198}. Invasion into the surrounding lung parenchyma or mediastinal structures can be a diagnostic finding of intimal sarcoma {18779732}. Also, a unilateral lesion within a pulmonary branch is more likely to be malignant, because chronic thromboemboli are usually multifocal {23648910}.

Pulmonary artery intimal sarcomas are rare and occur at approximately twice the rate of aortic intimal sarcomas. They are slightly more common in females (M:F ratio: ~0.7:1) {25393249}. The median age at diagnosis of intimal sarcoma of the pulmonary artery is 48 years {29962886; 8448740}. Pulmonary artery intimal sarcoma is present in 1–4% of pulmonary thromboendarterectomy specimens from patients thought to have chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension.

Discovery of frequent amplifications and gains in the 12q13-q14 region (containing MDM2 and CDK4) and amplification of PDGFRA and KIT (at 14q12), as detected by a range of molecular techniques including comparative genomic hybridization, array comparative genomic hybridization, FISH, and quantitative PCR, suggests that the MDM2 and PDGFR pathways may play a role in the pathogenesis of intimal sarcoma {11213836; 31480474; 20685895; 28501860}. Amplification/polysomy of EGFR has also been reported {17471466}.

In a series of cardiac sarcomas, intimal sarcoma was identified as the most frequent subtype, mainly on the basis of MDM2 amplification using FISH, PCR, and array comparative genomic hybridization {24625414}.

Intimal sarcomas are polypoid intraluminal masses attached to the wall and can resemble mucoid or gelatinous clots filling vascular lumina. Distal extension may show smooth tapering of the mass {18779732; 28040708}. Solid, fleshy tumour that completely occludes the vascular lumen is common in high-grade tumours, along with areas of haemorrhage and necrosis {16096408}.

Intimal sarcomas are mesenchymal neoplasms composed of spindle cells with varying degrees of atypia and variable cellularity. Higher-grade components show a high mitotic count, necrosis, and nuclear pleomorphism. Epithelioid morphology may be seen {16096408}. Lower-grade components are less cellular and can show myxoid change {7590704}. A small proportion of cases show heterologous elements in the form of osteosarcoma or chondrosarcoma. Rare tumours contain rhabdomyosarcomatous or angiosarcomatous features {8448740; 7590704; 10592050; 3055809}. Variable positivity for SMA is found, and some tumours exhibit positivity for desmin. Overall, the diagnosis does not require immunohistochemistry, but nuclear expression of MDM2 can be observed in ≥ 70% of cases and may be a defining feature {11213836; 20685895}.

FNA specimens of intraluminal sarcomas contain pleomorphic malignant spindled cells arranged in loosely cohesive clusters. Cell block material may be used for immunohistochemistry, FISH, or other ancillary techniques {30552756}.

MDM2 amplification has been observed in most pulmonary artery intimal sarcomas, along with immunohistochemical overexpression of the protein product, often coexisting with amplification of PDGFRA {11213836; 31480474; 28501860; 26725181; 31442826}.

Essential:

  • Presentation in the lumen of a large vessel of the pulmonary circulation
  • Primary high-grade sarcoma, with or without heterologous elements

Desirable:

  • MDM2 amplification (in selected cases)

The prognosis of pulmonary artery sarcoma is generally poor, with a mean survival time of 1–3 years {11213836; 8448740; 3055809; 18670310}. Rare intraluminal myofibroblastic tumours have a relatively good prognosis {18779732}.
